sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO at LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the shift from single-model AI to multi-agent systems for complex workflows. Highlighted how LangGraph enables reliable orchestration of agents with memory and human-in-the-loop capabilities, moving beyond simple prompt chaining.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Co-creator of Django, AI researcher & writer
sources.post_summary: Shared practical insights on building reliable AI tooling for developers. Covered the current limitations of agentic workflows and why most production systems still need strong guardrails and human oversight despite rapid progress.

sources.author: Clem Delangue
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO at Hugging Face
sources.post_summary: Posted about the rapid growth of open-source AI infrastructure and how Hugging Face is scaling inference and agent tooling. Emphasized the importance of open models and datasets for the next wave of developer-built AI applications.

sources.author: Swyx
sources.headline: Founder at Latent.Space, AI developer advocate
sources.post_summary: Wrote about the emerging category of 'AI-native' developer tools and how automation is changing software engineering workflows. Shared examples of agents that can write, test, and deploy code with minimal human intervention.

sources.author: Andrej Karpathy
sources.headline: AI researcher, former Director of AI at Tesla
sources.post_summary: Discussed the infrastructure challenges behind scaling agentic AI systems. Covered compute requirements, memory management, and why current cloud setups may not be optimal for long-running autonomous agents.

sources.author: Elena Voss
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations at Ramp
sources.post_summary: Discussed how her team built a unified GTM data model that connects marketing, sales, and CS metrics in one dashboard. Highlighted the shift from siloed reporting to a single source of truth that reduced forecast variance by 40%. Emphasized the role of RevOps in driving cross-functional alignment.

sources.author: Marcus Hale
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at OutboundOS
sources.post_summary: Shared a case study on automating outbound sequences using intent signals and AI enrichment. The system increased reply rates from 2.8% to 11.4% while cutting manual list building time by 70%. Stressed the importance of clean data pipelines before layering automation.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: GTM Engineer at Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how her team operationalized content-led growth by mapping blog topics to specific pipeline stages and measuring content-to-opportunity conversion. Showed a framework for scoring content assets based on revenue influence rather than just traffic or MQLs.

sources.author: David Kline
sources.headline: VP of Sales Operations at Deel
sources.post_summary: Outlined the process of building an internal GTM engineering function that owns tooling, data, and process automation. Covered how they reduced CRM admin time by 35% and improved lead-to-opportunity conversion through better routing logic.

sources.author: Lila Chen
sources.headline: Revenue Operations Lead at Vercel
sources.post_summary: Wrote about aligning content strategy with revenue goals by creating a content-to-pipeline attribution model. Shared how her team uses UTM governance and closed-loop reporting to measure which content types actually drive ARR.

sources.author: Alex Finn
sources.headline: Founder & Solo Builder @ ProductHunt Top 5 | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Shared his 90-day journey building and launching a solo AI productivity tool from scratch. Detailed the tech stack, first 1,000 users acquisition via Twitter and LinkedIn, and the decision to stay solo instead of raising. Highlighted key learnings around shipping fast and validating before polishing.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: Indie Hacker | Shipping Side Projects Full-Time
sources.post_summary: Posted a transparent breakdown of her transition from marketing manager to full-time indie developer. Walked through her first three micro-SaaS launches, revenue numbers, and the biggest mindset shifts required when moving from corporate to building in public.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Solo Developer | Building in Public | Ex-Finance
sources.post_summary: Documented shipping a developer tool in 6 weeks after leaving his finance role. Included weekly progress updates, user feedback loops, and how he used LinkedIn to find early beta users. Shared honest revenue figures and the challenges of customer support as a solo founder.

sources.author: Elena Rodriguez
sources.headline: Founder building AI agents | Previously PM at Stripe
sources.post_summary: Wrote about pivoting from product management to founding an AI agent startup. Detailed the decision to build in public on LinkedIn, how she validated the problem with 40 customer interviews, and the first version she shipped to early users within 8 weeks.

sources.author: David Kim
sources.headline: Solo Founder | Shipping MVPs in Public
sources.post_summary: Shared lessons from launching three failed products before his current profitable micro-SaaS. Focused on the importance of talking to users early, iterating in public, and how he uses weekly LinkedIn updates to stay accountable and attract collaborators.
